_note: How the procedural interiors are planned (world/innerMap/interiorPlanner.js). Each building type's required pieces are its INTERIOR_LAYOUTS furniture (world/innerMap/interiors.js; their coordinates only count the pieces); here are its size by wealth tier, its rooms (carved off the main room with inner walls and doorways: 'side' strips the depth of the house, split into k rooms; 'corner' rooms at the back or front), what each room takes of the required pieces ('type' or 'type:Name'), its extra pieces (by tier, chance and count), and its decor: 'items' set on tables, counters, desks and shelves (tile._decor), 'wall' hung on the walls facing into the room (tile._wallDecor). 'place' is each furniture type's placement rule: back, wall, side, corner, centre, far, bar, behind:bar, near:<type>, foot:bed, ends:table, rows, aisles, aisle, any. Sizes are [[minW,maxW],[minH,maxH]] in tiles, walls included; the building's own footprint leans the pick.
_exterior: Inside as it stands outside (interiorPlanner.js _exteriorOf, from the building's tile-composed design). Its width from its street frontage (frontage [narrow, wide] in tiles maps onto the type's size range about its tier, ± slack), its depth from its rows (depth [shallow, deep]); its door along the front wall where the facade's door is (doorMargin tiles off the corners); its front-wall windows where the facade's ground-floor windows are (window cells above upperRow are the upper storey's: they go on the floor above, and count its storeys for floors.js); a front with no windows has at most blindBackMax at the back; partyWalls styles stand shoulder to shoulder (no side windows). styles: an earth floor for the humbler old styles in the tiers given. wear: what is about the house (decor chances) by the street's era wear 0 fresh, 1 weathered, 2 old.
_household: Beds for who lives there (InnerMap.npcs whose home it is; types it applies to): a bed for each couple and each other grown one (adultAge and over), the children childrenPerBed to a bed (childBedPoor in a poor house: a straw pallet), a cradle for each infant (under infantAge); at most maxBeds beds and maxCradles cradles. A house with no street front to go by is planned the roomier the bigger its household (leanFrom..leanTo people lean its size from the bottom to the top of its tier range). Upstairs in the bedchamber where the house has one (data/buildingFloors.json), else on the ground floor. Extras marked household: true (a chance cradle, a spare bed) are left out where the household is known.

household._servants: Beds that are not the family's (world/innerMap/householdRooms.js): those in servantRooms (or named in servantBedNames) are the servants' cots — the house's servants (one living in: world/innerMap/townWork.js _liveInService, a grown servant with no spouse or children of their own, serving a house of liveInTypes) sleep there, a bedroll where there's no cot; apartRooms (guest rooms, a dormitory, a sergeant's room, or a floor of that room kind) are left to callers and lodgers.

_cellarTrips: Down to the cellar and back (world/innerMap/cellarTrips.js): a building's owner, its staff and the servants living in go down now and then to fetch what's kept there. Each slotMinutes a keeper may make a trip (chance by the cellar's room kind, data/buildingFloors.json cellars) of minutes long, within hours, never abed or at a meal; coming up, they carry what they fetched (carry, by cellar kind) for carrySecs. Never notTypes or notJobs.

ale_cellar.label: up from the cellar with a jug of ale

wine_cellar.label: up from the cellar with a bottle

store_cellar.label: up from the cellar with stores

root_cellar.label: up from the cellar with roots

_householdLife: The household in its own rooms (world/innerMap/householdRooms.js): by night each in their own bed (a couple side by side in one, the children paired in the children's beds, a babe in its cradle — the babe stays in it by day too); awake at home off work, the day's hearth-keeper (one grown one, by the day) tends the fire, a babe's parents mind the cradle, the children keep by the cradle, else childLikes. What they are seen doing there: hearth, cradleParent, cradleChild, inCradle.
_trades: What a house's people do (townsfolk occupations, data/townJobs.json; else their npc type) shows in it: each trade's pieces (placed first, in the main room, each with the decor on it given as 'decor'), its things on the furniture ('items', twice as likely as any other) and on the walls ('wall': its first hung once for certain, all in the main room's pool). _types: the building types it applies to; _max: trades shown per house.
_cultures: A culture's taste in its homes and halls (not its workshops): extras (pieces, by chance and tier, in the main room), items (on its furniture) and wall (hangings) added to every room's pool, wallChance a multiple of the tier's. Its floors and walls are the culture's own building materials (data/architecture.json); these are its furnishings.
_records: The insides of buildings kept once visited (world/interiorRecords.js, world/innerMap/persistInteriors.js): at most maxKept buildings in a world, the longest unvisited let go (planned afresh on the next visit).
_floors: The floors above the ground and the cellars under it (world/innerMap/floors.js _planFloor), planned like the ground floor: the ground floor's footprint and walls, entered by the stairs (kept clear, in the main room), no front door. Keyed by the room kind of data/buildingFloors.json (upperRooms, cellars), or '<type>.<kind>' for one type's own; each over `_upper` (every floor above) or `_cellar` (every cellar: no windows). The room's furniture (buildingFloors rooms, a household's beds counted in) are its required pieces, `take`n into rooms as on the ground floor; `extras`, `items`, `wall`, `place` as for types.
